dek: Free-data long-horizon context: dynamic rainbow bands, halving-cycle comparison, on-chain valuation and activity, leverage stress, and options positioning.
sourceNote: Coin Metrics Community API, OKX public market data, and Deribit public book summaries. Derived formulas are disclosed in each panel. No paid Glassnode cohort data is reproduced.

briefs.headline: A dynamic rainbow, with the assumptions left visible
briefs.lede: BTC finished 2026-10-12 at $81.8K, -0.72 standard deviations from the fitted long-run log trend.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Method. Paramaribo fits log10(BTC price) against log10(days since genesis) using daily Coin Metrics data from 2011 onward. The nine colored lines are half-standard-deviation residual steps around that fitted trend.

Use. This is a long-horizon valuation map, not a timing signal or a law of nature. The regression refits as new data arrive, so historical band placement can move.

charts.legend: Log scale · weekly observations · move across for band values

briefs.headline: Compare the current cycle without pretending the calendar must repeat
briefs.lede: The 2024 halving cycle is at day +905; its sampled price index is about 126, with halving day set to 100.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Method. Each cycle is aligned to its halving date and normalized to 100 on that date. Weekly observations run from 180 days before to 1,100 days after each halving.

Use. This reveals similarities and breaks in path, speed, and drawdown. Four completed or partial cycles are too few to treat repetition as a statistical certainty.

charts.title: BTC halving-cycle price index · halving day = 100

briefs.headline: Network cost basis is profitable, but not euphoric
briefs.lede: The community-data proxy puts network realized price near $53.8K and NUPL near 0.34 on 2026-10-12.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Method. Realized price proxy = PriceUSD ÷ MVRV. NUPL proxy = 1 − 1/MVRV, using Coin Metrics community MVRV.

Boundary. This is a network-wide proxy. It does not reproduce Glassnode's proprietary whale, shark, or shrimp cost-basis cohorts; those remain an explicit paid-data gap.

briefs.headline: Active addresses add adoption context, not a price target
briefs.lede: Bitcoin's seven-day average active-address count is about 631,370, +3.1% versus 30 observations earlier.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Method. Seven-day average of distinct active Bitcoin addresses from Coin Metrics. One user can control many addresses, and exchange batching can change the count.

Use. Look for persistent participation changes and price divergences; do not interpret a single-day spike as unique-user growth.

charts.title: BTC active addresses · 7-day average vs price

briefs.headline: A transparent leverage-stress percentile
briefs.lede: The Paramaribo 90-observation leverage-stress percentile is 81/100 through 2026-10-12.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Method. The score ranks seven-day OKX BTC open-interest growth plus the magnitude of any simultaneous seven-day BTC price decline against the prior 90 observations.

Boundary. This is Paramaribo's reproducible proxy, not the proprietary Alphractal indicator. Red means unusually fast leverage rebuilding during weak price; green means relatively cleared positioning.

charts.title: Paramaribo leverage-stress percentile [90 observations] vs BTC price

briefs.headline: Options open interest by expiry, not a one-number signal
briefs.lede: Across the next 11 listed expiries, Deribit put/call open interest is 0.60; reference BTC underlying is about $83.7K.
briefs.bodyHtml:
Snapshot. Public Deribit book summaries at 2026-10-13 20:19 UTC. Open interest is aggregated in BTC by listed expiry for calls and puts.

Use. Concentrated expiry interest identifies dates where hedging and dealer positioning may matter. It does not reveal direction by itself and is not a historical options-OI series.
